correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3 and N=2n, the graph distance profile is f(k)=min(k,n+1-k) for 0<=k<=n, extended by reflection. Directly computing its circular second difference gives two positive corners at 0,n and parity-dependent negative corners, yielding every nonconstant Fourier eigenvalue. All even frequencies have nonpositive eigenvalues; among odd positive frequencies j=3 is uniquely largest up to reflection. The exceptional n=3 1D mode and the parity expansions are checked analytically. A standalone pure-Python breadth-first-search/Fourier checker passed 298986 supplementary finite assertions for n=3..60 plus selected asymptotic tests. The finite experiments are not claimed to prove the universal statement.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact shortest-path QEC and top Fourier eigenspace, not only its terminology, against foundational constant-row-sum QEC results, 2023 full Möbius-ladder resistance-matrix results, general graph distance-spectrum texts, 2024 bipartite QE classifications, indexed family tables, targeted searches, and recoverable existing claims. The six-vertex complete-bipartite specialization is explicitly prior. None of the materially inspected results supplied the all-order parity formula and maximizer; historical priority remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older geodesic distance-spectrum treatment of Möbius ladders with different indexing or terminology may have escaped targeted searches; novelty is best-knowledge, not exhaustive proof.
A 2026 published revision of the resistance-distance preprint could contain material not compared here; the 2023 lawful open-access original was inspected directly.
Only finite numerical checks accompany an analytic all-size proof; they do not establish independent validation.

value.rationale: Computes an unknown-in-inspected-literature, natural quadratic embedding constant of a standard, vertex-transitive cubic graph family at every order. The exact maximizing Fourier support exhibits structural rigidity; its parity asymptotic gives two different 1/n corrections about a common linear growth law. This supplies quantitative Hilbert-embedding obstruction and a sharp benchmark when comparing graph geodesic and resistance metrics. A singleton computation or routine substitution would not supply this complete parity-resolved spectral classification.
